_meta.indication: PRADAXA is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: RE-LY (Randomized Evaluation of Long-term Anticoagulant Therapy)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, parallel-group, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial comparing 2 blinded doses of dabigatran etexilate (110 mg bid, 150 mg bid) to open-label adjusted-dose warfarin (target INR 2.0-3.0); a PROBE (Prospective Randomized Open trial with Blinded outcome Evaluation) hybrid design, non-inferiority margin 1.46.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor (previous ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, or TIA; heart failure; age >75 years; or age >65 with diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, or hypertension).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to first occurrence of stroke (both ischemic and hemorrhagic) or systemic embolism.
pivotal_trials.result: For stroke/SEE, dabigatran 150 mg bid was non-inferior and superior to warfarin: HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.52, 0.81), p=0.0001 for non-inferiority and p=0.0001 for superiority; 134 vs 202 events. The 110 mg dose: HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.74, 1.10).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>15%) are gastritis-like symptoms and bleeding. Patients on PRADAXA 150 mg had increased gastrointestinal adverse reactions (35% vs 24% on warfarin). In RE-LY, major bleed rate was 3.3% vs 3.6% warfarin (HR 0.93), any bleed 16.6% vs 18.4%, intracranial hemorrhage 0.3% vs 0.8% (HR 0.41); adverse reactions leading to discontinuation were 21% for PRADAXA 150 mg vs 16% for warfarin.
target_moa: Dabigatran etexilate is a small-molecule prodrug of dabigatran, a competitive, reversible, direct thrombin inhibitor; by inhibiting thrombin (which converts fibrinogen to fibrin) it prevents thrombus formation and acts as an anticoagulant.

rems.type: The REMS, submitted December 15, 2009 and amended October 18, 2010, is approved and consists of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: Referred to the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (CRDAC) on September 20, 2010, which voted 9 'yes', 0 'no', 0 'abstain' that dabigatran should be approved.

description.text: Added treatment of DVT and PE after parenteral anticoagulant therapy and reduction of risk of DVT/PE recurrence

citations.quote:
- For the treatment of deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients who have been treated with a parenteral anticoagulant for 5-10 days.
- To reduce the risk of recurrence of DVT and PE in patients who have been previously treated.

description.text: Added new indication: prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in patients who have undergone hip replacement surgery (and registered the 110 mg capsule strength)

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for the registration of the 110 mg capsule strength and a new indication: Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in patients who have undergone hip replacement surgery.

description.text: Added treatment and reduction of recurrence of VTE in pediatric patients 8 to less than 18 years treated with a parenteral anticoagulant for at least 5 days

citations.quote:
- Treatment of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in pediatric patients 8 to less than 18 years of age who have been treated with a parenteral anticoagulant for at least 5 days
- To reduce the risk of recurrence of VTE in pediatric patients 8 to less than 18 years of age who have been previously treated

summary.text: PRADAXA (dabigatran etexilate) was approved via a traditional NDA on the basis of the single pivotal phase 3 trial RE-LY; the Division recommended approval of the 150 mg capsule and the CRDAC voted 9-0 in favor. Approval included a REMS (Medication Guide) due to bleeding risk and two required postmarketing in vitro transporter studies.

citations.quote: The Division of Cardiovascular and Renal Products is recommending approval of dabigatran etexilate, 150 mg capsules for oral administration, for reducing the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF).
The protocol for a single pivotal phase 3 trial (RE-LY) was submitted for Special Protocol Assessment, and the Division provided comments on 7/11/2005.
The REMS consists of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

requirement.text: An in vitro study profiling dabigatran as a substrate or inhibitor of a panel of drug Solute Carrier (SLC) transporters (OATPs, OATs, and OCTs).
